body: Mason: Noble couldn't sign in with Google on 2026-10-15, though Kimani had added his exact email on Access, and nobody could see why without Netlify's function log. Build a sign-in log admins can read in the tool: (1) the Identity gate (server/identity-events.ts) records every decision (event, provider, allowed or not, via; for a refusal only the domain, as today) to a small table; (2) the sign-in page catches the error Google or Identity hands back in the URL (error, error_description, e.g. admin_policy_enforced or access_denied) and records it through an unauthenticated, rate-limited, size-capped endpoint; (3) Access shows the last 100 lines. That tells a Google-side block (Casa's Workspace refusing Netlify's Google app) from our gate refusing. Additive migration with a fresh timestamp. PR to claude/main; never merge. Sign "— Mason (CR-6)". Mark Dispatch Ledger line casa-r12-2 delivered when the PR opens.
note: Superseded by Dispatch 22 (casa-r13-8), which keeps this line's URL-error capture.
summary: A sign-in log admins can read, so refused sign-ins explain themselves.
title: Follow-up: a sign-in log in the tool
